  1308→// InitializeSession creates session state for a new session or updates an existing one.
  1309→// This implements the optional SessionInitializer interface.
  1310→// Called during UserPromptSubmit to allow git hooks to detect active sessions.
  1311→//
  1312→// If the session already exists and HEAD has moved (e.g., user committed), updates
  1313→// BaseCommit to the new HEAD so future checkpoints go to the correct shadow branch.
  1314→//
  1315→// If there's an existing shadow branch with commits from a different session ID,
  1316→// returns a SessionIDConflictError to prevent orphaning existing session work.
  1317→//
  1318→// agentType is the human-readable name of the agent (e.g., "Claude Code").
  1319→// transcriptPath is the path to the live transcript file (for mid-session commit detection).
  1320→// userPrompt is the user's prompt text (stored truncated as FirstPrompt for display).
  1321→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) InitializeSession(sessionID string, agentType agent.AgentType, transcriptPath string, userPrompt string) error {
  1322→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
  1323→	if err != nil {
  1324→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
  1325→	}
  1326→
  1327→	// Check if session already exists
  1328→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
  1329→	if err != nil {
  1330→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to check session state: %w", err)
  1331→	}
  1332→
  1333→	if state != nil && state.BaseCommit != "" {
  1334→		// Session is fully initialized — apply phase transition for TurnStart
  1335→		TransitionAndLog(state, session.EventTurnStart, session.TransitionContext{})
  1336→
  1337→		// Generate a new TurnID for each turn (correlates carry-forward checkpoints)
  1338→		turnID, err := id.Generate()
  1339→		if err != nil {
  1340→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate turn ID: %w", err)
  1341→		}
  1342→		state.TurnID = turnID.String()
  1343→
  1344→		// Backfill AgentType if empty or set to the generic default "Agent"
  1345→		if !isSpecificAgentType(state.AgentType) && agentType != "" {
  1346→			state.AgentType = agentType
  1347→		}
  1348→
  1349→		// Backfill FirstPrompt if empty (for sessions created before the first_prompt field was added)
  1350→		if state.FirstPrompt == "" && userPrompt != "" {
  1351→			state.FirstPrompt = truncatePromptForStorage(userPrompt)
  1352→		}
  1353→
  1354→		// Update transcript path if provided (may change on session resume)
  1355→		if transcriptPath != "" && state.TranscriptPath != transcriptPath {
  1356→			state.TranscriptPath = transcriptPath
  1357→		}
  1358→
  1359→		// Clear checkpoint IDs on every new prompt.
  1360→		// LastCheckpointID is set during PostCommit, cleared at new prompt.
  1361→		// TurnCheckpointIDs tracks mid-turn checkpoints for stop-time finalization.
  1362→		state.LastCheckpointID = ""
  1363→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1364→
  1365→		// Calculate attribution at prompt start (BEFORE agent makes any changes)
  1366→		// This captures user edits since the last checkpoint (or base commit for first prompt).
  1367→		// IMPORTANT: Always calculate attribution, even for the first checkpoint, to capture
  1368→		// user edits made before the first prompt. The inner CalculatePromptAttribution handles
  1369→		// nil lastCheckpointTree by falling back to baseTree.
  1370→		promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
  1371→		state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr
  1372→
  1373→		// Check if HEAD has moved (user pulled/rebased or committed)
  1374→		// migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded handles renaming the shadow branch and updating state.BaseCommit
  1375→		if _, err := s.migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded(repo, state); err != nil {
  1376→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check/migrate shadow branch: %w", err)
  1377→		}
  1378→
  1379→		if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
  1380→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to update session state: %w", err)
  1381→		}
  1382→		return nil
  1383→	}
  1384→	// If state exists but BaseCommit is empty, it's a partial state from concurrent warning
  1385→	// Continue below to properly initialize it
  1386→
  1387→	// Initialize new session
  1388→	state, err = s.initializeSession(repo, sessionID, agentType, transcriptPath, userPrompt)
  1389→	if err != nil {
  1390→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize session: %w", err)
  1391→	}
  1392→
  1393→	// Apply phase transition: new session starts as ACTIVE
  1394→	TransitionAndLog(state, session.EventTurnStart, session.TransitionContext{})
  1395→
  1396→	// Calculate attribution for pre-prompt edits
  1397→	// This captures any user edits made before the first prompt
  1398→	promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
  1399→	state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr
  1400→	if err = s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
  1401→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save attribution: %w", err)
  1402→	}
  1403→
  1404→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Initialized shadow session: %s\n", sessionID)
  1405→	return nil
  1406→}
  1407→
  1408→// calculatePromptAttributionAtStart calculates attribution at prompt start (before agent runs).
  1409→// This captures user changes since the last checkpoint - no filtering needed since
  1410→// the agent hasn't made any changes yet.
  1411→//
  1412→// IMPORTANT: This reads from the worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
  1413→// captures in checkpoints. If we read staged content but checkpoints capture worktree content,
  1414→// unstaged changes would be in the checkpoint but not counted in PromptAttribution, causing
  1415→// them to be incorrectly attributed to the agent later.
  1416→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(
  1417→	repo *git.Repository,
  1418→	state *SessionState,
  1419→) PromptAttribution {
  1420→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "attribution")
  1421→	nextCheckpointNum := state.StepCount + 1
  1422→	result := PromptAttribution{CheckpointNumber: nextCheckpointNum}
  1423→
  1424→	// Get last checkpoint tree from shadow branch (if it exists)
  1425→	// For the first checkpoint, no shadow branch exists yet - this is fine,
  1426→	// CalculatePromptAttribution will use baseTree as the reference instead.
  1427→	var lastCheckpointTree *object.Tree
  1428→	shadowBranchName := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
  1429→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
  1430→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
  1431→	if err != nil {
  1432→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: no shadow branch yet (first checkpoint)",
  1433→			slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName))
  1434→		// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
  1435→	} else {
  1436→		shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
  1437→		if err != nil {
  1438→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow commit",
  1439→				slog.String("shadow_ref", ref.Hash().String()),
  1440→				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1441→			// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
  1442→		} else {
  1443→			lastCheckpointTree, err = shadowCommit.Tree()
  1444→			if err != nil {
  1445→				logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow tree",
  1446→					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1447→				// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
  1448→			}
  1449→		}
  1450→	}
  1451→
  1452→	// Get base tree for agent lines calculation
  1453→	var baseTree *object.Tree
  1454→	if baseCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(state.BaseCommit)); err == nil {
  1455→		if tree, treeErr := baseCommit.Tree(); treeErr == nil {
  1456→			baseTree = tree
  1457→		} else {
  1458→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: base tree unavailable",
  1459→				slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()))
  1460→		}
  1461→	} else {
  1462→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: base commit unavailable",
  1463→			slog.String("base_commit", state.BaseCommit),
  1464→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1465→	}
  1466→
  1467→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1468→	if err != nil {
  1469→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree",
  1470→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1471→		return result
  1472→	}
  1473→
  1474→	// Get worktree status to find ALL changed files
  1475→	status, err := worktree.Status()
  1476→	if err != nil {
  1477→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree status",
  1478→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
  1479→		return result
  1480→	}
  1481→
  1482→	worktreeRoot := worktree.Filesystem.Root()
  1483→
  1484→	// Build map of changed files with their worktree content
  1485→	// IMPORTANT: We read from worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
  1486→	// captures in checkpoints. This ensures attribution is consistent.
  1487→	changedFiles := make(map[string]string)
  1488→	for filePath, fileStatus := range status {
  1489→		// Skip unmodified files
  1490→		if fileStatus.Worktree == git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging == git.Unmodified {
  1491→			continue
  1492→		}
  1493→		// Skip .entire metadata directory (session data, not user code)
  1494→		if strings.HasPrefix(filePath, paths.EntireMetadataDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(filePath, ".entire/") {
  1495→			continue
  1496→		}
  1497→
  1498→		// Always read from worktree to match checkpoint behavior
  1499→		fullPath := filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, filePath)
  1500→		var content string
  1501→		if data, err := os.ReadFile(fullPath); err == nil { //nolint:gosec // filePath is from git worktree status
  1502→			// Use git's binary detection algorithm (matches getFileContent behavior).
  1503→			// Binary files are excluded from line-based attribution calculations.
  1504→			isBinary, binErr := binary.IsBinary(bytes.NewReader(data))
  1505→			if binErr == nil && !isBinary {
  1506→				content = string(data)
  1507→			}
  1508→		}
  1509→		// else: file deleted, unreadable, or binary - content remains empty string
  1510→
  1511→		changedFiles[filePath] = content
  1512→	}
  1513→
  1514→	// Use CalculatePromptAttribution from manual_commit_attribution.go
  1515→	result = CalculatePromptAttribution(baseTree, lastCheckpointTree, changedFiles, nextCheckpointNum)
  1516→
  1517→	return result
  1518→}

  1520→// getStagedFiles returns a list of files staged for commit.
  1521→func getStagedFiles(repo *git.Repository) []string {
  1522→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1523→	if err != nil {
  1524→		return nil
  1525→	}
  1526→
  1527→	status, err := worktree.Status()
  1528→	if err != nil {
  1529→		return nil
  1530→	}
  1531→
  1532→	var staged []string
  1533→	for path, fileStatus := range status {
  1534→		// Check if file is staged (in index)
  1535→		if fileStatus.Staging != git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging != git.Untracked {
  1536→			staged = append(staged, path)
  1537→		}
  1538→	}
  1539→	return staged
  1540→}

  1542→// getLastPrompt retrieves the most recent user prompt from a session's shadow branch.
  1543→// Returns empty string if no prompt can be retrieved.
  1544→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) getLastPrompt(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) string {
  1545→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
  1546→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
  1547→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)

  1549→		return ""
  1550→	}
  1551→
  1552→	// Extract session data to get prompts for commit message generation
  1553→	// Pass agent type to handle different transcript formats (JSONL for Claude, JSON for Gemini)
  1554→	// Pass 0 for checkpointTranscriptStart since we're extracting all prompts, not calculating token usage
  1555→	sessionData, err := s.extractSessionData(repo, ref.Hash(), state.SessionID, nil, state.AgentType, "", 0)
  1556→	if err != nil || len(sessionData.Prompts) == 0 {
  1557→		return ""
  1558→	}

  1561→	return sessionData.Prompts[len(sessionData.Prompts)-1]

  1564→// HandleTurnEnd dispatches strategy-specific actions emitted when an agent turn ends.
  1565→// The primary job is to finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.
  1566→//
  1567→// During a turn, PostCommit writes provisional transcript data (whatever was available
  1568→// at commit time). HandleTurnEnd replaces that with the complete session transcript
  1569→// (from prompt to stop event), ensuring every checkpoint has the full context.
  1570→//
  1571→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
  1572→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) HandleTurnEnd(state *SessionState) error {
  1573→	// Finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.
  1574→	//
  1575→	// IMPORTANT: This is best-effort - errors are logged but don't fail the hook.
  1576→	// Failing here would prevent session cleanup and could leave state inconsistent.
  1577→	// The provisional transcript from PostCommit is already persisted, so the
  1578→	// checkpoint isn't lost - it just won't have the complete transcript.
  1579→	errCount := s.finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(state)
  1580→	if errCount > 0 {
  1581→		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
  1582→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "HandleTurnEnd completed with errors (best-effort)",
  1583→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1584→			slog.Int("error_count", errCount),
  1585→		)
  1586→	}
  1587→	return nil
  1588→}
  1589→
  1590→// finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints replaces the provisional transcript in each checkpoint
  1591→// created during this turn with the full session transcript.
  1592→//
  1593→// This is called at turn end (stop hook). During the turn, PostCommit wrote whatever
  1594→// transcript was available at commit time. Now we have the complete transcript and
  1595→// replace it so every checkpoint has the full prompt-to-stop context.
  1596→//
  1597→// Returns the number of errors encountered (best-effort: continues processing on error).
  1598→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(state *SessionState) int {
  1599→	if len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs) == 0 {
  1600→		return 0 // No mid-turn commits to finalize
  1601→	}
  1602→
  1603→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
  1604→
  1605→	logging.Info(logCtx, "finalizing turn checkpoints with full transcript",
  1606→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1607→		slog.Int("checkpoint_count", len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs)),
  1608→	)
  1609→
  1610→	errCount := 0
  1611→
  1612→	// Read full transcript from live transcript file
  1613→	if state.TranscriptPath == "" {
  1614→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: no transcript path, skipping",
  1615→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1616→		)
  1617→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1618→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1619→	}
  1620→
  1621→	fullTranscript, err := os.ReadFile(state.TranscriptPath)
  1622→	if err != nil || len(fullTranscript) == 0 {
  1623→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: failed to read transcript, skipping",
  1624→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1625→			slog.String("transcript_path", state.TranscriptPath),
  1626→		)
  1627→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1628→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1629→	}
  1630→
  1631→	// Extract prompts and context from the full transcript
  1632→	prompts := extractUserPrompts(state.AgentType, string(fullTranscript))
  1633→	contextBytes := generateContextFromPrompts(prompts)
  1634→
  1635→	// Redact secrets before writing — matches WriteCommitted behavior.
  1636→	// The live transcript on disk contains raw content; redaction must happen
  1637→	// before anything is persisted to the metadata branch.
  1638→	fullTranscript, err = redact.JSONLBytes(fullTranscript)
  1639→	if err != nil {
  1640→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: transcript redaction failed, skipping",
  1641→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1642→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1643→		)
  1644→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1645→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1646→	}
  1647→	for i, p := range prompts {
  1648→		prompts[i] = redact.String(p)
  1649→	}
  1650→	contextBytes = redact.Bytes(contextBytes)
  1651→
  1652→	// Open repository and create checkpoint store
  1653→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
  1654→	if err != nil {
  1655→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: failed to open repository",
  1656→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1657→		)
  1658→		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1659→		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
  1660→	}
  1661→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)
  1662→
  1663→	// Update each checkpoint with the full transcript
  1664→	for _, cpIDStr := range state.TurnCheckpointIDs {
  1665→		cpID, parseErr := id.NewCheckpointID(cpIDStr)
  1666→		if parseErr != nil {
  1667→			logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: invalid checkpoint ID, skipping",
  1668→				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
  1669→				slog.String("error", parseErr.Error()),
  1670→			)
  1671→			errCount++
  1672→			continue
  1673→		}
  1674→
  1675→		updateErr := store.UpdateCommitted(context.Background(), checkpoint.UpdateCommittedOptions{
  1676→			CheckpointID: cpID,
  1677→			SessionID:    state.SessionID,
  1678→			Transcript:   fullTranscript,
  1679→			Prompts:      prompts,
  1680→			Context:      contextBytes,
  1681→			Agent:        state.AgentType,
  1682→		})
  1683→		if updateErr != nil {
  1684→			logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: failed to update checkpoint",
  1685→				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
  1686→				slog.String("error", updateErr.Error()),
  1687→			)
  1688→			errCount++
  1689→			continue
  1690→		}
  1691→
  1692→		logging.Info(logCtx, "finalize: checkpoint updated with full transcript",
  1693→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
  1694→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1695→		)
  1696→	}
  1697→
  1698→	// Update transcript start and clear turn checkpoint IDs
  1699→	fullTranscriptLines := countTranscriptItems(state.AgentType, string(fullTranscript))
  1700→	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = fullTranscriptLines
  1701→	state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
  1702→
  1703→	return errCount
  1704→}

  1706→// filesChangedInCommit returns the set of files changed in a commit by diffing against its parent.
  1707→func filesChangedInCommit(commit *object.Commit) map[string]struct{} {
  1708→	result := make(map[string]struct{})
  1709→
  1710→	commitTree, err := commit.Tree()

  1763→// carryForwardToNewShadowBranch creates a new shadow branch at the current HEAD
  1764→// containing the remaining uncommitted files and all session metadata.
  1765→// This enables the next commit to get its own unique checkpoint.
  1766→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(
  1767→	logCtx context.Context,
  1768→	repo *git.Repository,
  1769→	state *SessionState,
  1770→	remainingFiles []string,
  1771→) {
  1772→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)

  1775→	// only needs to preserve file content for comparison - not the transcript.
  1776→	// Including the transcript would cause sessionHasNewContent to always return true
  1777→	// because CheckpointTranscriptStart is reset to 0 for carry-forward.
  1778→	result, err := store.WriteTemporary(context.Background(), checkpoint.WriteTemporaryOptions{
  1779→		SessionID:         state.SessionID,
  1780→		BaseCommit:        state.BaseCommit,
  1781→		WorktreeID:        state.WorktreeID,
  1782→		ModifiedFiles:     remainingFiles,
  1783→		MetadataDir:       "",
  1784→		MetadataDirAbs:    "",
  1785→		CommitMessage:     "carry forward: uncommitted session files",
  1786→		IsFirstCheckpoint: false,
  1787→	})

  1790→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1791→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1792→		)
  1793→		return
  1794→	}

  1796→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward skipped (no changes)",
  1797→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1798→		)
  1799→		return
  1800→	}

  1802→	// Update state for the carry-forward checkpoint.
  1803→	// CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0 is intentional: each checkpoint is self-contained with
  1804→	// the full transcript. This trades storage efficiency for simplicity:

  1806→	//   multiple checkpoints to understand the session history

   701→// condenseAndUpdateState runs condensation for a session and updates state afterward.
   702→// Returns true if condensation succeeded.
   703→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) condenseAndUpdateState(
   704→	logCtx context.Context,
   705→	repo *git.Repository,
   706→	checkpointID id.CheckpointID,
   707→	state *SessionState,
   708→	head *plumbing.Reference,
   709→	shadowBranchName string,
   710→	shadowBranchesToDelete map[string]struct{},
   711→) bool {
   712→	result, err := s.CondenseSession(repo, checkpointID, state)
   713→	if err != nil {
   714→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: condensation failed for session %s: %v\n",
   715→			state.SessionID, err)
   716→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: condensation failed",
   717→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   718→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   719→		)
   720→		return false
   721→	}
   722→
   723→	// Track this shadow branch for cleanup
   724→	shadowBranchesToDelete[shadowBranchName] = struct{}{}
   725→
   726→	// Update session state for the new base commit
   727→	newHead := head.Hash().String()
   728→	state.BaseCommit = newHead
   729→	state.AttributionBaseCommit = newHead
   730→	state.StepCount = 0
   731→	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = result.TotalTranscriptLines
   732→
   733→	// Clear attribution tracking — condensation already used these values
   734→	state.PromptAttributions = nil
   735→	state.PendingPromptAttribution = nil
   736→	state.FilesTouched = nil
   737→
   738→	// Save checkpoint ID so subsequent commits can reuse it (e.g., amend restores trailer)
   739→	state.LastCheckpointID = checkpointID
   740→
   741→	shortID := state.SessionID
   742→	if len(shortID) > 8 {
   743→		shortID = shortID[:8]
   744→	}
   745→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Condensed session %s: %s (%d checkpoints)\n",
   746→		shortID, result.CheckpointID, result.CheckpointsCount)
   747→
   748→	logging.Info(logCtx, "session condensed",
   749→		slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   750→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", result.CheckpointID.String()),
   751→		slog.Int("checkpoints_condensed", result.CheckpointsCount),
   752→		slog.Int("transcript_lines", result.TotalTranscriptLines),
   753→	)

   755→	return true
   756→}
   757→
   758→// updateBaseCommitIfChanged updates BaseCommit to newHead if it changed.
   759→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) updateBaseCommitIfChanged(logCtx context.Context, state *SessionState, newHead string) {
   760→	if state.BaseCommit != newHead {
   761→		state.BaseCommit = newHead
   762→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: updated BaseCommit",
   763→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   764→			slog.String("new_head", truncateHash(newHead)),
   765→		)
   766→	}
   767→}
   768→
   769→// postCommitUpdateBaseCommitOnly updates BaseCommit for all sessions on the current
   770→// worktree when a commit has no Entire-Checkpoint trailer. This prevents BaseCommit
   771→// from going stale, which would cause future PrepareCommitMsg calls to skip the
   772→// session (BaseCommit != currentHeadHash filter).
   773→//
   774→// Unlike the full PostCommit flow, this does NOT fire EventGitCommit or trigger
   775→// condensation — it only keeps BaseCommit in sync with HEAD.
   776→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) postCommitUpdateBaseCommitOnly(logCtx context.Context, head *plumbing.Reference) {
   777→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
   778→	if err != nil {
   779→		return // Silent failure — hooks must be resilient
   780→	}
   781→
   782→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath)
   783→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   784→		return
   785→	}
   786→
   787→	newHead := head.Hash().String()
   788→	for _, state := range sessions {
   789→		// Only update active sessions. Idle/ended sessions are kept around for
   790→		// LastCheckpointID reuse and should not be advanced to HEAD.
   791→		if !state.Phase.IsActive() {
   792→			continue
   793→		}
   794→		if state.BaseCommit != newHead {
   795→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit (no trailer): updating BaseCommit",
   796→				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   797→				slog.String("old_base", truncateHash(state.BaseCommit)),
   798→				slog.String("new_head", truncateHash(newHead)),
   799→			)
   800→			state.BaseCommit = newHead
   801→			if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   802→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: failed to update session state: %v\n", err)
   803→			}
   804→		}
   805→	}
   806→}
   807→
   808→// truncateHash safely truncates a git hash to 7 chars for logging.
   809→func truncateHash(h string) string {
   810→	if len(h) > 7 {
   811→		return h[:7]
   812→	}
   813→	return h
   814→}
   815→
   816→// filterSessionsWithNewContent returns sessions that have new transcript content
   817→// beyond what was already condensed.
   818→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo *git.Repository, sessions []*SessionState) []*SessionState {
   819→	var result []*SessionState
   820→
   821→	for _, state := range sessions {
   822→		hasNew, err := s.sessionHasNewContent(repo, state)
   823→		if err != nil {
   824→			// On error, include the session (fail open for hooks)
   825→			result = append(result, state)
   826→			continue
   827→		}
   828→		if hasNew {
   829→			result = append(result, state)
   830→		}
   831→	}
   832→
   833→	return result
   834→}
   835→
   836→// sessionHasNewContent checks if a session has new transcript content
   837→// beyond what was already condensed.
   838→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) sessionHasNewContent(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {
   839→	// Get shadow branch
   840→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   841→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   842→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   843→	if err != nil {
   844→		// No shadow branch means no Stop has happened since the last condensation.
   845→		// However, the agent may have done work (including commits) without a Stop.
   846→		// Check the live transcript to detect this scenario.
   847→		return s.sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript(repo, state)
   848→	}

1763→// carryForwardToNewShadowBranch creates a new shadow branch at the current HEAD
  1764→// containing the remaining uncommitted files and all session metadata.
  1765→// This enables the next commit to get its own unique checkpoint.
  1766→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(
  1767→	logCtx context.Context,
  1768→	repo *git.Repository,
  1769→	state *SessionState,
  1770→	remainingFiles []string,
  1771→) {
  1772→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)
  1773→
  1774→	// Don't include metadata directory in carry-forward. The carry-forward branch
  1775→	// only needs to preserve file content for comparison - not the transcript.
  1776→	// Including the transcript would cause sessionHasNewContent to always return true
  1777→	// because CheckpointTranscriptStart is reset to 0 for carry-forward.
  1778→	result, err := store.WriteTemporary(context.Background(), checkpoint.WriteTemporaryOptions{
  1779→		SessionID:         state.SessionID,
  1780→		BaseCommit:        state.BaseCommit,
  1781→		WorktreeID:        state.WorktreeID,
  1782→		ModifiedFiles:     remainingFiles,
  1783→		MetadataDir:       "",
  1784→		MetadataDirAbs:    "",
  1785→		CommitMessage:     "carry forward: uncommitted session files",
  1786→		IsFirstCheckpoint: false,
  1787→	})
  1788→	if err != nil {
  1789→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward failed",
  1790→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1791→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1792→		)
  1793→		return
  1794→	}
  1795→	if result.Skipped {
  1796→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward skipped (no changes)",
  1797→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
  1798→		)
  1799→		return
  1800→	}
  1801→
  1802→	// Update state for the carry-forward checkpoint.
  1803→	// CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0 is intentional: each checkpoint is self-contained with
  1804→	// the full transcript. This trades storage efficiency for simplicity:
  1805→	// - Pro: Each checkpoint is independently readable without needing to stitch together
  1806→	//   multiple checkpoints to understand the session history
  1807→	// - Con: For long sessions with multiple partial commits, each checkpoint includes
  1808→	//   the full transcript, which could be large
  1809→	// An alternative would be incremental checkpoints (only new content since last condensation),
  1810→	// but this would complicate checkpoint retrieval and require careful tracking of dependencies.

  1813→	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0

  1817→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),

  1819→	)

   838→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) sessionHasNewContent(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {

   841→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   842→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   843→	if err != nil {
   844→		// No shadow branch means no Stop has happened since the last condensation.
   845→		// However, the agent may have done work (including commits) without a Stop.
   846→		// Check the live transcript to detect this scenario.

   853→	}
   854→
   855→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   856→	if err != nil {
   857→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   858→	}
   859→
   860→	// Look for transcript file
   861→	metadataDir := paths.EntireMetadataDir + "/" + state.SessionID
   862→	var transcriptLines int
   863→	var hasTranscriptFile bool
   864→

   866→		hasTranscriptFile = true
   867→		if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   868→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptItems(state.AgentType, content)
   869→		}
   870→	} else if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy); fileErr == nil {
   871→		hasTranscriptFile = true
   872→		if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   873→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptItems(state.AgentType, content)
   874→		}
   875→	}
   876→
   877→	// If shadow branch exists but has no transcript (e.g., carry-forward from mid-session commit),
   878→	// check if the session has FilesTouched. Carry-forward sets FilesTouched with remaining files.
   879→	if !hasTranscriptFile {

106→// CondenseSession condenses a session's shadow branch to permanent storage.
   107→// checkpointID is the 12-hex-char value from the Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
   108→// Metadata is stored at sharded path: <checkpoint_id[:2]>/<checkpoint_id[2:]>/
   109→// Uses checkpoint.GitStore.WriteCommitted for the git operations.
   110→//
   111→// For mid-session commits (no Stop/SaveChanges called yet), the shadow branch may not exist.
   112→// In this case, data is extracted from the live transcript instead.
   113→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CondenseSession(repo *git.Repository, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, state *SessionState) (*CondenseResult, error) {
   114→	// Get shadow branch (may not exist for mid-session commits)
   115→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   116→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   117→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   118→	hasShadowBranch := err == nil
   119→
   120→	var sessionData *ExtractedSessionData
   121→	if hasShadowBranch {
   122→		// Extract session data from the shadow branch (with live transcript fallback).
   123→		// Use tracked files from session state instead of collecting all files from tree.
   124→		// Pass agent type to handle different transcript formats (JSONL for Claude, JSON for Gemini).
   125→		// Pass live transcript path so condensation reads the current file rather than a
   126→		// potentially stale shadow branch copy (SaveChanges may have been skipped if the
   127→		// last turn had no code changes).
   128→		// Pass CheckpointTranscriptStart for accurate token calculation (line offset for Claude, message index for Gemini).
   129→		sessionData, err = s.extractSessionData(repo, ref.Hash(), state.SessionID, state.FilesTouched, state.AgentType, state.TranscriptPath, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   130→		if err != nil {
   131→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to extract session data: %w", err)
   132→		}
   133→	} else {
   134→		// No shadow branch: mid-session commit before Stop/SaveChanges.
   135→		// Extract data directly from live transcript.
   136→		if state.TranscriptPath == "" {
   137→			return nil, errors.New("shadow branch not found and no live transcript available")
   138→		}
   139→		sessionData, err = s.extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript(state)
   140→		if err != nil {

   147→	if err != nil {

   149→	}
   150→
   151→	// Get author info
   152→	authorName, authorEmail := GetGitAuthorFromRepo(repo)
   153→	// Attribution calculation requires shadow branch reference; skip if mid-session commit
   154→	var attribution *cpkg.InitialAttribution
   155→	if hasShadowBranch {
   156→		attribution = calculateSessionAttributions(repo, ref, sessionData, state)
   157→	}
   158→	// Get current branch name
   159→	branchName := GetCurrentBranchName(repo)
   160→
   161→	// Generate summary if enabled
   162→	var summary *cpkg.Summary
   163→	if settings.IsSummarizeEnabled() && len(sessionData.Transcript) > 0 {
   164→		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "attribution")
   165→		summarizeCtx := logging.WithComponent(logCtx, "summarize")
   166→
   167→		// Scope transcript to this checkpoint's portion.
   168→		// For Claude Code (JSONL), CheckpointTranscriptStart is a line offset.
   169→		// For Gemini (JSON), CheckpointTranscriptStart is a message index.
   170→		var scopedTranscript []byte
   171→		if state.AgentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
   172→			scopedTranscript = geminicli.SliceFromMessage(sessionData.Transcript, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   173→		} else {
   174→			scopedTranscript = transcript.SliceFromLine(sessionData.Transcript, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   175→		}
   176→		if len(scopedTranscript) > 0 {
   177→			var err error
   178→			summary, err = summarize.GenerateFromTranscript(summarizeCtx, scopedTranscript, sessionData.FilesTouched, state.AgentType, nil)
   179→			if err != nil {
   180→				logging.Warn(summarizeCtx, "summary generation failed",
   181→					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   182→					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   183→				// Continue without summary - non-blocking
   184→			} else {
   185→				logging.Info(summarizeCtx, "summary generated",
   186→					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID))
   187→			}
   188→		}
   189→	}
   190→
   191→	// Write checkpoint metadata using the checkpoint store
   192→	if err := store.WriteCommitted(context.Background(), cpkg.WriteCommittedOptions{
   193→		CheckpointID:                checkpointID,
   194→		SessionID:                   state.SessionID,
   195→		Strategy:                    StrategyNameManualCommit,
   196→		Branch:                      branchName,

## Bug 1 Fix: Second Checkpoint Metadata Missing

**Root Cause:** For IDLE sessions with carry-forward, `PostCommit` called `sessionHasNewContent()` which checked if **staged** files overlap with remaining files. But in post-commit, files are already committed - not staged! So `getStagedFiles()` returned empty and the check failed, preventing condensation.

**Fix (Two Parts):**

1. **`manual_commit_condensation.go:200`** - Added `TranscriptPath` to `WriteCommittedOptions`:
   ```go
   TranscriptPath: state.TranscriptPath,  // for carry-forward transcript fallback
   ```

2. **`manual_commit_hooks.go:556-580`** - Added explicit carry-forward detection:
   ```go
   // Carry-forward: FilesTouched > 0 AND CheckpointTranscriptStart == 0
   if len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 && state.CheckpointTranscriptStart == 0 {
       hasNew = true  // Let content-aware check decide
   }
   ```
   This bypasses `sessionHasNewContent()` which incorrectly uses staged files in post-commit.

3. **`deferred_finalization_test.go:362`** - Fixed test to use `SimulateUserPromptSubmitWithTranscriptPath` so transcript path is set in session state.

**Key Insight:** Carry-forward resets `CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0` and creates a shadow branch with files but no transcript. Regular IDLE sessions have `CheckpointTranscriptStart > 0`. This distinction lets us detect carry-forward.

content.text:
All tests pass and the code is clean. Let me provide a summary of the fixes:

## Bug Fix Summary

### Bug 2: files_touched incorrect in multi-commit scenarios
**Root cause:** For mid-session commits during an ACTIVE turn, `CondenseSession` extracted `files_touched` from the transcript which included ALL files mentioned in the transcript from the offset onwards, not just files in the specific commit.

**Fix:**
- Added `committedFiles map[string]struct{}` parameter to `CondenseSession`
- Filter extracted `FilesTouched` to only include files actually in `committedFiles`
- Updated `condenseAndUpdateState` to pass `committedFileSet`

**Files changed:**
- `manual_commit_condensation.go` - Added parameter and filtering logic
- `manual_commit_hooks.go` - Updated calls to pass `committedFileSet`
- `manual_commit_test.go` - Updated test calls

### Bug 3: Content-aware overlap detection not applied in PrepareCommitMsg
**Root cause:** The `sessionHasNewContent` function returned `true` based solely on transcript growth, without checking if the staged files actually contained the session's content. This caused checkpoint trailers to be added even when the user had reverted and replaced the agent's work with completely different content.

**Fix:**
- Modified `sessionHasNewContent` to perform content-aware overlap checking
- When transcript has grown, also verify that staged files overlap with session's files AND have matching content
- If user reverted and wrote different content (content mismatch), no checkpoint trailer is added

**Files changed:**
- `manual_commit_hooks.go` - Added content-aware checking in `sessionHasNewContent`

All unit tests and integration tests pass.

    if strings.HasPrefix(line, pattern) || line == pattern {
        return true
    }
}
```

The check `line == pattern` is wrong. 

Looking at the user content more carefully:
```go
"package main\n\n// Completely different implementation\nfunc C() { panic(\"manual\") }\n"
```

Breaking it down line by line: `package main` gets filtered as trivial, the empty line is too short, but `// Completely different implementation` is a comment with substantial length that wouldn't be marked trivial. The function line also starts with `func ` so it's skipped. This means the comment line is the only significant content, and if it's not in the agent's version, there shouldn't be overlap detected.

The agent's content is much simpler:
```go
"package main\n\nfunc C() {}\n"
```

All lines here are either trivial (package and func declarations) or empty. When `hasSignificantContentOverlap` finds no significant lines in the agent's content, it returns `true` unconditionally—that's the flaw. The function assumes any file overlap is acceptable when there's nothing substantial to compare against, but it should actually require the user's significant content to be present.

The real problem is the fallback behavior. If the agent generated only boilerplate code, we shouldn't automatically accept overlap with user content that contains actual logic or comments. Instead, we need to verify that the user's meaningful lines actually appear in what the agent produced. If they don't match, there's no real overlap—just coincidental file structure.

1. `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript` returned empty `FilesTouched`
2. The filtering removed all files

Let me think about what happens for the third commit:
1. Agent creates file3.go and commits
2. PostCommit runs
3. `CondenseSession` is called with `committedFiles = {file3.go}`
4. `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript` extracts files from transcript
5. My filtering code filters to only files in `committedFiles`

The issue might be that `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript` is not finding file3.go in the transcript portion. Let me check what `state.CheckpointTranscriptStart` is set to after the second commit.

Actually, let me trace through more carefully:

After first commit (file1.go):
- `state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = TotalTranscriptLines` (say, 10)

After second commit (file2.go):
- `state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = TotalTranscriptLines` (say, 20)

Third commit (file3.go):
- `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript` is called


- It reads the full transcript
- `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(path, 20)` extracts files from line 20 onwards

If the agent created all three files and committed them rapidly, the transcript might have been written all at once with all file modifications. So `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(path, 20)` might not find file3.go if file3.go creation was written before line 20. This could be a transcript growth timing issue where the transcript is written as the agent works, and if the agent creates all files quickly and commits them, the transcript might have all creations before the first commit's condensation. But the second and third commits happen after the first commit, so the transcript should have grown between them.

When PostCommit runs, there should be additional content in the transcript if the agent continued working. I need to determine whether this is a race condition or a fundamental problem with how the transcript offset tracking works. Looking at the test output, checkpoint 0 expects file3.go but gets nil, checkpoint 1 expects file2.go, and checkpoint 2 expects file1.go—suggesting the files are being detected in reverse order or the offset calculation is off.

The checkpoints come back most recent first, so checkpoint 0 (file3.go, the third commit) failed validation while checkpoints 1 and 2 passed. This points to an issue specific to the final commit's processing. After the third commit, the agent might have stopped and triggered a Stop hook that corrupted the state, though in the mid-turn scenario there shouldn't be a Stop between commits.

I need to understand what differs about that last commit. The `committedFiles` filtering could be too strict, or there's a gap between how integration tests mock the transcript upfront versus how e2e tests build it incrementally as the agent executes. Since I can't easily run e2e tests without a real agent, I should verify the integration test `TestShadow_MultipleCommits_SameActiveTurn` still passes—it covers the same three-file, three-commit scenario and should validate the logic works.

The real difference might be in transcript extraction. For the third commit mid-turn, `state.FilesTouched` could be empty since no Stop event has fired yet, forcing `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript` to pull from the transcript. If that extraction fails or returns nothing, `files_touched` ends up nil. My filtering condition then skips the block entirely because `sessionData.FilesTouched` is empty, leaving `FilesTouched` as nil instead of using the committed files. The solution might be to handle the case where `sessionData.FilesTouched` is empty differently—perhaps falling back to `committedFiles` or adjusting the filtering logic.

All tests pass. Let me provide a summary of all the bug fixes:

## Summary of Bug Fixes

### Bug 2: files_touched incorrect in multi-commit scenarios
**Root cause:** For mid-session commits, `extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript` extracted ALL files mentioned in the transcript from the offset onwards, not just files in the specific commit.

**Fix:**
1. Added `committedFiles map[string]struct{}` parameter to `CondenseSession`
2. Filter extracted `FilesTouched` to only include files in `committedFiles`
3. Added fallback: if extraction returns empty but `committedFiles` is available, use `committedFiles` as `FilesTouched`

**Files changed:**
- `manual_commit_condensation.go` - Added filtering logic and fallback
- `manual_commit_hooks.go` - Pass `committedFileSet` to `condenseAndUpdateState`
- `manual_commit_test.go` - Updated test calls

### Bug 3: Content-aware overlap detection not rejecting "reverted and replaced" scenarios
**Root cause:** `sessionHasNewContent` returned `true` based solely on transcript growth, without checking if staged files actually contained the session's content.

**Fix:**
1. Modified `sessionHasNewContent` to perform content-aware overlap checking when transcript has grown
2. Implemented `hasSignificantContentOverlap` to compare file contents line by line:
   - Identifies "significant" lines (non-trivial, ≥10 chars)
   - Matches if any significant line appears in both files
   - Properly handles edge cases (both trivial, one trivial, etc.)
3. Updated `stagedFilesOverlapWithContent` to read and compare actual file contents when hashes differ

**Files changed:**
- `manual_commit_hooks.go` - Added content-aware checking in `sessionHasNewContent`
- `content_overlap.go` - Added `hasSignificantContentOverlap`, `isTrivialLine`, and content reading logic

### Key behaviors after fixes:
- **Multi-commit scenarios**: Each checkpoint gets `files_touched` with only the files from that specific commit
- **Partial staging**: User keeps some agent content → checkpoint created
- **Reverted and replaced**: User completely replaces agent content → no checkpoint trailer
- **Fallback safety**: If transcript extraction fails, uses committed files as `files_touched`

    13→// getAllChangedFilesBetweenTrees returns a list of all files that differ between two trees.
    14→// This includes files that were added, modified, or deleted in either tree.
    15→// Uses git blob hashes for efficient comparison without reading file contents.
    16→func getAllChangedFilesBetweenTrees(tree1, tree2 *object.Tree) []string {
    17→	if tree1 == nil && tree2 == nil {
    18→		return nil
    19→	}
    20→
    21→	// Build hash maps for each tree - O(n) iteration, no content reading
    22→	tree1Hashes := make(map[string]string)
    23→	tree2Hashes := make(map[string]string)
    24→
    25→	if tree1 != nil {
    26→		//nolint:errcheck // Errors ignored - just collecting file hashes for diff comparison
    27→		_ = tree1.Files().ForEach(func(f *object.File) error {
    28→			tree1Hashes[f.Name] = f.Hash.String()
    29→			return nil
    30→		})
    31→	}
    32→
    33→	if tree2 != nil {
    34→		//nolint:errcheck // Errors ignored - just collecting file hashes for diff comparison
    35→		_ = tree2.Files().ForEach(func(f *object.File) error {
    36→			tree2Hashes[f.Name] = f.Hash.String()
    37→			return nil
    38→		})
    39→	}
    40→
    41→	// Find changed files by comparing hashes (much faster than content comparison)
    42→	var changed []string
    43→
    44→	// Check files in tree1 - either modified or deleted in tree2
    45→	for path, hash1 := range tree1Hashes {
    46→		if hash2, exists := tree2Hashes[path]; !exists || hash1 != hash2 {
    47→			changed = append(changed, path)
    48→		}
    49→	}
    50→
    51→	// Check files only in tree2 (added files)
    52→	for path := range tree2Hashes {
    53→		if _, exists := tree1Hashes[path]; !exists {
    54→			changed = append(changed, path)
    55→		}
    56→	}
    57→
    58→	return changed
    59→}
    60→
    61→// getFileContent retrieves the content of a file from a tree.
    62→// Returns empty string if the file doesn't exist, can't be read, or is a binary file.
    63→//
    64→// Binary files are silently excluded from attribution calculations because line-based
    65→// diffing doesn't apply to binary content. This means binary files (images, compiled
    66→// binaries, etc.) won't appear in attribution metrics even if they were added or modified.
    67→// This is intentional - attribution measures code contributions via line counting,
    68→// which only makes sense for text files.
    69→//
    70→// Uses go-git's IsBinary() which implements git's binary detection algorithm.
    71→//
    72→// TODO: Consider tracking binary file counts separately (e.g., BinaryFilesChanged field)
    73→// to provide visibility into non-text file modifications.
    74→func getFileContent(tree *object.Tree, path string) string {
    75→	if tree == nil {
    76→		return ""
    77→	}
    78→

    88→	}

    91→	if err != nil {

    97→
    98→// diffLines compares two strings and returns line-level diff stats.
    99→// Returns (unchanged, added, removed) line counts.
   100→func diffLines(checkpointContent, committedContent string) (unchanged, added, removed int) {
   101→	// Handle edge cases
   102→	if checkpointContent == committedContent {
   103→		return countLinesStr(committedContent), 0, 0
   104→	}
   105→	if checkpointContent == "" {
   106→		return 0, countLinesStr(committedContent), 0
   107→	}
   108→	if committedContent == "" {
   109→		return 0, 0, countLinesStr(checkpointContent)
   110→	}
   111→
   112→	dmp := diffmatchpatch.New()
   113→
   114→	// Convert to line-based diff using DiffLinesToChars/DiffCharsToLines pattern
   115→	text1, text2, lineArray := dmp.DiffLinesToChars(checkpointContent, committedContent)
   116→	diffs := dmp.DiffMain(text1, text2, false)
   117→	diffs = dmp.DiffCharsToLines(diffs, lineArray)
   118→
   119→	for _, d := range diffs {
   120→		lines := countLinesStr(d.Text)
   121→		switch d.Type {
   122→		case diffmatchpatch.DiffEqual:
   123→			unchanged += lines
   124→		case diffmatchpatch.DiffInsert:
   125→			added += lines
   126→		case diffmatchpatch.DiffDelete:
   127→			removed += lines
   128→		}
   129→	}
   130→
   131→	return unchanged, added, removed
   132→}
   133→
   134→// countLinesStr returns the number of lines in a string.
   135→// An empty string has 0 lines. A string without newlines has 1 line.
   136→// This is used for both file content and diff text segments.
   137→func countLinesStr(content string) int {
   138→	if content == "" {
   139→		return 0
   140→	}
   141→	lines := strings.Count(content, "\n")
   142→	// If content doesn't end with newline, add 1 for the last line
   143→	if !strings.HasSuffix(content, "\n") {
   144→		lines++
   145→	}
   146→	return lines
   147→}
   148→
   149→// CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated computes final attribution using accumulated prompt data.
   150→// This provides more accurate attribution than tree-only comparison because it captures
   151→// user edits that happened between checkpoints (which would otherwise be mixed into the
   152→// checkpoint snapshots).
   153→//
   154→// The calculation:
   155→// 1. Sum user edits from PromptAttributions (captured at each prompt start)
   156→// 2. Add user edits after the final checkpoint (shadow → head diff)
   157→// 3. Calculate agent lines from base → shadow
   158→// 4. Estimate user self-modifications vs agent modifications using per-file tracking
   159→// 5. Compute percentages
   160→//
   161→// Note: Binary files (detected by null bytes) are silently excluded from attribution
   162→// calculations since line-based diffing only applies to text files.
   163→//
   164→// See docs/architecture/attribution.md for details on the per-file tracking approach.
   165→func CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated(
   166→	baseTree *object.Tree,
   167→	shadowTree *object.Tree,
   168→	headTree *object.Tree,
   169→	filesTouched []string,
   170→	promptAttributions []PromptAttribution,
   171→) *checkpoint.InitialAttribution {
   172→	if len(filesTouched) == 0 {
   173→		return nil
   174→	}
   175→
   176→	// Sum accumulated user lines from prompt attributions
   177→	// Also aggregate per-file user additions for accurate modification tracking
   178→	var accumulatedUserAdded, accumulatedUserRemoved int
   179→	accumulatedUserAddedPerFile := make(map[string]int)
   180→	for _, pa := range promptAttributions {
   181→		accumulatedUserAdded += pa.UserLinesAdded
   182→		accumulatedUserRemoved += pa.UserLinesRemoved
   183→		// Merge per-file data from all prompt attributions
   184→		for filePath, added := range pa.UserAddedPerFile {
   185→			accumulatedUserAddedPerFile[filePath] += added
   186→		}
   187→	}
   188→
   189→	// Calculate attribution for agent-touched files
   190→	// IMPORTANT: shadowTree is a snapshot of the worktree at checkpoint time,
   191→	// which includes both agent work AND accumulated user edits (to agent-touched files).
   192→	// So base→shadow diff = (agent work + accumulated user work to these files).
   193→	var totalAgentAndUserWork int
   194→	var postCheckpointUserAdded, postCheckpointUserRemoved int
   195→	postCheckpointUserRemovedPerFile := make(map[string]int)
   196→
   197→	for _, filePath := range filesTouched {
   198→		baseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)
   199→		shadowContent := getFileContent(shadowTree, filePath)
   200→		headContent := getFileContent(headTree, filePath)
   201→
   202→		// Total work in shadow: base → shadow (agent + accumulated user work for this file)
   203→		_, workAdded, _ := diffLines(baseContent, shadowContent)
   204→		totalAgentAndUserWork += workAdded
   205→
   206→		// Post-checkpoint user edits: shadow → head (only post-checkpoint edits for this file)
   207→		_, postUserAdded, postUserRemoved := diffLines(shadowContent, headContent)
   208→		postCheckpointUserAdded += postUserAdded
   209→		postCheckpointUserRemoved += postUserRemoved
   210→
   211→		// Track per-file removals for self-modification estimation
   212→		if postUserRemoved > 0 {
   213→			postCheckpointUserRemovedPerFile[filePath] = postUserRemoved
   214→		}
   215→	}
   216→
   217→	// Calculate total user edits to non-agent files (files not in filesTouched)
   218→	// These files are not in the shadow tree, so base→head captures ALL their user edits
   219→	nonAgentFiles := getAllChangedFilesBetweenTrees(baseTree, headTree)
   220→	var allUserEditsToNonAgentFiles int
   221→	for _, filePath := range nonAgentFiles {
   222→		if slices.Contains(filesTouched, filePath) {
   223→			continue // Skip agent-touched files
   224→		}
   225→
   226→		baseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)
   227→		headContent := getFileContent(headTree, filePath)
   228→		_, userAdded, _ := diffLines(baseContent, headContent)
   229→		allUserEditsToNonAgentFiles += userAdded
   230→	}
   231→
   232→	// Separate accumulated edits by file type using per-file tracking data.
   233→	// This is precise because accumulatedUserAddedPerFile tells us exactly which files
   234→	// the user edited between checkpoints.
   235→	var accumulatedToAgentFiles, accumulatedToNonAgentFiles int
   236→	for filePath, added := range accumulatedUserAddedPerFile {
   237→		if slices.Contains(filesTouched, filePath) {
   238→			accumulatedToAgentFiles += added
   239→		} else {
   240→			accumulatedToNonAgentFiles += added
   241→		}
   242→	}
   243→
   244→	// Agent work = (base→shadow for agent files) - (accumulated user edits to agent files only)
   245→	totalAgentAdded := max(0, totalAgentAndUserWork-accumulatedToAgentFiles)
   246→

   248→	postToNonAgentFiles := max(0, allUserEditsToNonAgentFiles-accumulatedToNonAgentFiles)
   249→
   250→	// Total user contribution = accumulated (all files) + post-checkpoint (agent files) + post-checkpoint (non-agent files)
   251→	totalUserAdded := accumulatedUserAdded + postCheckpointUserAdded + postToNonAgentFiles
   252→	totalUserRemoved := accumulatedUserRemoved + postCheckpointUserRemoved
   253→

   255→	// Lines that were both added and removed are treated as modifications.
   256→	totalHumanModified := min(totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved)
   257→
   258→	// Estimate user self-modifications using per-file tracking (see docs/architecture/attribution.md)
   259→	// When a user removes lines from a file, assume they're removing their own lines first (LIFO).
   260→	// Only after exhausting their own additions should we count removals as targeting agent lines.
   261→	userSelfModified := estimateUserSelfModifications(accumulatedUserAddedPerFile, postCheckpointUserRemovedPerFile)

   263→	// humanModifiedAgent = modifications that targeted agent lines (not user's own lines)
   264→	humanModifiedAgent := max(0, totalHumanModified-userSelfModified)
   265→
   266→	// Remaining modifications are user self-modifications (user edited their own code)
   267→	// These should NOT be subtracted from agent lines
   268→	pureUserAdded := totalUserAdded - totalHumanModified
   269→	pureUserRemoved := totalUserRemoved - totalHumanModified

   280→		// the attribution percentage is only meaningful for commits that add code.
   281→		totalCommitted = max(0, totalAgentAdded)

   331→//   - lastCheckpointTree: the tree from the previous checkpoint (nil if first checkpoint)
   332→//   - worktreeFiles: map of file path → current worktree content for files that changed
   333→//   - checkpointNumber: which checkpoint we're about to create (1-indexed)

   337→// previous checkpoint to measure cumulative agent work against.
   338→//
   339→// Note: Binary files (detected by null bytes) in reference trees are silently excluded
   340→// from attribution calculations since line-based diffing only applies to text files.
   341→func CalculatePromptAttribution(

   343→	lastCheckpointTree *object.Tree,

   345→	checkpointNumber int,

   354→	}

   364→		baseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)

   367→		// These are changes since the last checkpoint that the agent didn't make
   368→		_, userAdded, userRemoved := diffLines(referenceContent, worktreeContent)
   369→		result.UserLinesAdded += userAdded
   370→		result.UserLinesRemoved += userRemoved
   371→

   373→		// This enables distinguishing user self-modifications from agent modifications.
   374→		if userAdded > 0 {
   375→			result.UserAddedPerFile[filePath] = userAdded
   376→		}
   377→
   378→		// Agent lines so far: diff(base, lastCheckpoint)
   379→		// Only calculate if we have a previous checkpoint

   384→			result.AgentLinesRemoved += agentRemoved
   385→		}
   386→	}
   387→

   - Fix: Added `committedFiles` parameter to `CondenseSession` to filter `files_touched`
   - Files modified: `manual_commit_condensation.go`, `manual_commit_hooks.go`, `manual_commit_test.go`

3. **Bug 3 Investigation and Fix**:
   - Issue: Content-aware overlap detection not rejecting "reverted and replaced" scenarios
   - Root cause: `sessionHasNewContent` returned `true` based solely on transcript growth without checking content
   - Fix: Added content-aware checking in `sessionHasNewContent`
   - Created `hasSignificantContentOverlap` function in `content_overlap.go`

4. **E2E Test Failures Analysis**:
   - Multiple e2e tests failed after initial fixes
   - Scenario 3: `files_touched: <nil>` for last checkpoint
   - Scenario 5, 7: Content check too strict (rejecting partial staging)

   - The `stagedFilesOverlapWithContent` function needed to read actual file contents and compare
   - Implemented `hasSignificantContentOverlap` to compare line-by-line
   - Added fallback in condensation to use `committedFiles` when extraction fails

   - Found `diffLines` function in `manual_commit_attribution.go` that uses `diffmatchpatch`
   - Tried refactoring to use `diffLines` but it was too permissive (treated boilerplate as overlap)

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - 1:1 checkpoint model (one checkpoint per commit)
   - Shadow branch (`entire/checkpoints/v1`) for metadata storage
   - Carry-forward mechanism for uncommitted files
   - Content-aware overlap detection to distinguish:
     - Partial staging (user kept some agent content) → checkpoint created
     - Reverted and replaced (completely different content) → no checkpoint
   - `committedFileSet` - files changed in a specific commit
   - `state.FilesTouched` - files modified by the session
   - `state.CheckpointTranscriptStart` - transcript position for incremental extraction
   - `diffLines` function using `github.com/sergi/go-diff/diffmatchpatch` for line-level diffing

     - Added `committedFiles` parameter to `CondenseSession`

     - Added fallback to use `committedFiles` when extraction fails
     ```go
     // For 1:1 checkpoint model: filter files_touched to only include files actually
     // committed in this specific commit.
     if len(committedFiles) > 0 {
         if len(sessionData.FilesTouched) > 0 {
             filtered := make([]string, 0, len(sessionData.FilesTouched))
             for _, f := range sessionData.FilesTouched {
                 if _, ok := committedFiles[f]; ok {
                     filtered = append(filtered, f)
                 }
             }
             sessionData.FilesTouched = filtered
         }
         // If extraction failed or returned empty, use committedFiles as fallback.
         if len(sessionData.FilesTouched) == 0 {
             sessionData.FilesTouched = make([]string, 0, len(committedFiles))
             for f := range committedFiles {

     if transcriptLines <= state.CheckpointTranscriptStart {

     if len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 {

     - Added `hasSignificantContentOverlap` function (currently being refined):
     ```go
     // hasSignificantContentOverlap checks if two file contents share significant lines.
     func hasSignificantContentOverlap(stagedContent, shadowContent string) bool {
         shadowLines := extractSignificantLines(shadowContent)
         stagedLines := extractSignificantLines(stagedContent)
         // If both have no significant lines, no meaningful overlap
         if len(shadowLines) == 0 && len(stagedLines) == 0 {

         }
         // ... additional checks ...
         for line := range stagedLines {

             }

All tests pass, including the previously failing `TestShadow_RevertedFiles_ManualEditNoCheckpoint` test.

**Summary of fixes:**

1. **Bug 2 (files_touched incorrect)**: Added `committedFiles` parameter to `CondenseSession` to filter `files_touched` to only include files from the specific commit, with a fallback for extraction failures.

2. **Bug 3 (content-aware overlap detection)**: 
   - Added content comparison in `sessionHasNewContent` via `stagedFilesOverlapWithContent`
   - Implemented `hasSignificantContentOverlap` that compares file contents line-by-line, filtering out trivial lines (boilerplate like `package`, `import`, `func`, single braces/parens, comments)
   - This correctly distinguishes:
     - **Partial staging** (user kept some agent content) → checkpoint created
     - **Reverted and replaced** (completely different content) → no checkpoint

The `diffLines` function from attribution code was too permissive because it treats any matching text (including boilerplate like `package main`) as overlap. The manual line comparison approach with trivial line filtering correctly handles the reverted-files scenario.

content.text:
**Bug 2: `files_touched` incorrect in multi-commit scenarios**

When multiple commits happen during an ACTIVE turn, each checkpoint's `files_touched` was getting all files from the transcript instead of just the files in that specific commit.

**Fix:** Added `committedFiles` parameter to `CondenseSession` that filters `files_touched` to only include files actually committed in each specific commit.

---

**Bug 3: Content-aware overlap not rejecting reverted files**

When a user reverts agent-written content and replaces it with completely different content, a checkpoint was still being created (because the filename matched).

**Fix:** Added `hasSignificantContentOverlap` in `content_overlap.go` that compares actual file content line-by-line, filtering out trivial lines (boilerplate like `package`, `import`, braces). Now only creates a checkpoint if the staged content shares meaningful lines with the shadow branch content.

---

**Files changed:**
- `manual_commit_condensation.go` - `committedFiles` parameter + filtering logic
- `manual_commit_hooks.go` - pass `committedFiles` through `condenseAndUpdateState`
- `content_overlap.go` - `hasSignificantContentOverlap` function
- `manual_commit_test.go` - updated test call sites

203→// PrepareCommitMsg is called by the git prepare-commit-msg hook.
   204→// Adds an Entire-Checkpoint trailer to the commit message with a stable checkpoint ID.
   205→// Only adds a trailer if there's actually new session content to condense.
   206→// The actual condensation happens in PostCommit - if the user removes the trailer,
   207→// the commit will not be linked to the session (useful for "manual" commits).
   208→// For amended commits, preserves the existing checkpoint ID.
   209→//
   210→// The source parameter indicates how the commit was initiated:
   211→//   - "" or "template": normal editor flow - adds trailer with explanatory comment
   212→//   - "message": using -m or -F flag - prompts user interactively via /dev/tty
   213→//   - "merge", "squash": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated messages)
   214→//   - "commit": amend operation - preserves existing trailer or restores from LastCheckpointID
   215→//
   216→
   217→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile string, source string) error {
   218→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")

   226→		)
   227→		return nil

   230→	// Skip for merge and squash sources

   236→			slog.String("source", source),
   237→		)
   238→		return nil
   239→	}
   240→
   241→	// Handle amend (source="commit") separately: preserve or restore trailer
   242→	if source == "commit" {
   243→		return s.handleAmendCommitMsg(logCtx, commitMsgFile)
   244→	}

The `GitStash` function looks fine - it just runs `git stash`. But `git stash` only stashes **tracked** files by default. If the files B and C are untracked (new files created by the agent), they won't be stashed.

Looking at the test:1. Agent creates A, B, C (new files, untracked)
2. User commits A (A becomes tracked, B and C remain untracked)
3. User runs `git stash` (doesn't stash B and C because they're untracked)

That's the issue! `git stash` doesn't stash untracked files by default. You need `git stash -u` or `git stash --include-untracked` to stash untracked files.

This is actually a test bug, not a bug in our code. But the user is right that we need to fix it. Let me update the `GitStash` function to include untracked files.

content.text:
All tests pass. Here's a summary of the new e2e tests I added for scenarios with existing files:

**New tests in `scenario_checkpoint_workflows_test.go`:**

1. **`TestE2E_ExistingFiles_ModifyAndCommit`**
   - Agent modifies an existing tracked file
   - User commits the modification
   - Verifies checkpoint is created

2. **`TestE2E_ExistingFiles_StashModifications`**
   - Agent modifies two existing tracked files
   - User commits one, stashes the other
   - User pops stash and commits the second file
   - Verifies both get separate checkpoints
   - Tests that standard `git stash` (without `-u`) works for tracked file modifications

3. **`TestE2E_ExistingFiles_SplitCommits`**
   - Agent modifies three existing files (model.go, view.go, controller.go)
   - User commits each separately
   - Validates each checkpoint has correct `files_touched`
   - Similar to Scenario 4 but with modifications instead of new files

4. **`TestE2E_ExistingFiles_RevertModification`**
   - Agent modifies existing file (adds Multiply function)
   - User reverts and writes different changes (adds Subtract function)
   - Verifies content-aware detection prevents checkpoint trailer
   - Tests Bug 3 fix with existing files

5. **`TestE2E_ExistingFiles_MixedNewAndModified`**
   - Agent creates new files AND modifies existing file in same session
   - User commits modifications and new files separately
   - Verifies both commits get checkpoints

Also added `GetLatestCheckpointID()` helper that returns the checkpoint from HEAD commit (empty string if none) for test convenience.

content.text:
**The Carry-Forward Scenario:**

1. Agent creates files A, B, C, D in one prompt
2. User commits only A and B → first checkpoint created
3. Files C and D are "carried forward" - they're still uncommitted but tracked in `state.FilesTouched`
4. User commits C and D → should get second checkpoint

**What was happening:**

After the first commit + condensation:
- The shadow branch gets updated/moved to point to the condensed checkpoint
- `state.FilesTouched` is updated to `[C, D]` (the remaining uncommitted files)
- But files C and D were **never written to the shadow branch tree** - they only existed in the working directory

When the second commit happens, `stagedFilesOverlapWithContent` does:
```go
// Check if file C is in the shadow branch tree
shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File("C")
if err != nil {
    // File not found in shadow tree
    continue  // ← OLD: Skip this file, check next one
}
```

Since C and D don't exist in the shadow branch tree, they were being skipped. If no files matched, the function returned `false` (no overlap), so no checkpoint was created.

**The fix:**

```go
shadowFile, err := shadowTree.File(stagedPath)
if err != nil {
    // File is in filesTouched but NOT in shadow tree.
    // This is a carry-forward file: session tracked it, but shadow 
    // branch was moved after condensation. Trust filesTouched.
    return true  // ← NEW: Count as overlap
}
```

The key insight: if a file is in `state.FilesTouched`, the session DID touch it. Even if it's not in the shadow branch tree (because the branch was reset after condensation), we should trust `FilesTouched` and create a checkpoint for it.

**Test scenario** (no new content):1. Agent works, saves checkpoint to shadow branch (including test.txt)


2. User commits test.txt with checkpoint trailer

**Carry-forward scenario**:

2. Agent stops (all files saved to shadow branch)
3. User commits only A, B with checkpoint trailer
4. PostCommit condenses and carries forward C, D to new shadow branch
5. User commits C, D with checkpoint trailer
6. PostCommit SHOULD condense (these files weren't in the first checkpoint)

The transcript length hasn't changed, and `FilesTouched` gets updated to only include uncommitted files. When the user commits the remaining files, PostCommit should condense those as well.

In carry-forward, `FilesTouched` tracks files that weren't part of the previous commit—these are the new files to condense.    446→// GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory walks backwards from HEAD and returns
   447→// the checkpoint ID from the first commit with an Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
   448→// Returns an error if no checkpoint trailer is found in any commit.
   449→func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory() (string, error) {
   450→	env.T.Helper()
   451→
   452→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   453→	if err != nil {
   454→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   455→	}
   456→
   457→	head, err := repo.Head()
   458→	if err != nil {
   459→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get HEAD: %v", err)
   460→	}
   461→
   462→	commitIter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: head.Hash()})
   463→	if err != nil {
   464→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to iterate commits: %v", err)
   465→	}
   466→
   467→	var checkpointID string
   468→	//nolint:errcheck,gosec // ForEach callback returns error to stop iteration, not a real error
   469→	commitIter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
   470→		// Look for Entire-Checkpoint trailer
   471→		for _, line := range strings.Split(c.Message, "\n") {
   472→			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   473→			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:") {
   474→				checkpointID = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:"))
   475→				return errors.New("stop iteration")
   476→			}
   477→		}
   478→		return nil
   479→	})
   480→
   481→	if checkpointID == "" {
   482→		return "", errors.New("no commit with Entire-Checkpoint trailer found in history")
   483→	}
   484→
   485→	return checkpointID, nil
   486→}

   740→// ValidateCheckpoint performs comprehensive validation of a checkpoint on the metadata branch.
   741→func (env *TestEnv) ValidateCheckpoint(v CheckpointValidation) {
   742→	env.T.Helper()
   743→
   744→	metadataBranch := "entire/checkpoints/v1"
   745→
   746→	// Compute sharded path: <id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/
   747→	if len(v.CheckpointID) < 3 {
   748→		env.T.Fatalf("Checkpoint ID too short: %s", v.CheckpointID)
   749→	}
   750→	shardedPath := v.CheckpointID[:2] + "/" + v.CheckpointID[2:]
   751→
   752→	// Validate root metadata.json exists and has expected fields
   753→	summaryPath := shardedPath + "/metadata.json"
   754→	summaryContent, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(metadataBranch, summaryPath)
   755→	if !found {
   756→		env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary not found at %s", summaryPath)
   757→	} else {
   758→		var summary map[string]any
   759→		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(summaryContent), &summary); err != nil {
   760→			env.T.Errorf("Failed to parse CheckpointSummary: %v", err)
   761→		} else {
   762→			// Validate checkpoint_id
   763→			if cpID, ok := summary["checkpoint_id"].(string); !ok || cpID != v.CheckpointID {

   424→			ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{"combo_a.go", "combo_b.go", "combo_c.go"}, // Full prompt 1 transcript

   537→// TestE2E_ContentAwareOverlap_RevertAndReplace tests content-aware overlap detection
   538→// when user reverts session changes and writes different content.
   539→//
   540→// Content-Aware Overlap Detection:
   541→// - Agent creates file X with content "hello"
   542→// - User reverts X (git checkout -- X)
   543→// - User writes completely different content
   544→// - User commits
   545→// - Content mismatch → NO checkpoint trailer added
   546→func TestE2E_ContentAwareOverlap_RevertAndReplace(t *testing.T) {
   547→	t.Parallel()
   548→
   549→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, "manual-commit")
   550→
   551→	// Agent creates a file
   552→	t.Log("Agent creating file with specific content")
   553→	createPrompt := `Create a file called overlap_test.go with this exact content:
   554→package main
   555→
   556→func OverlapOriginal() string {
   557→	return "original content from agent"
   558→}
   559→
   560→Create only this file.`
   561→
   562→	result, err := env.RunAgent(createPrompt)
   563→	require.NoError(t, err)
   564→	AssertAgentSuccess(t, result, err)
   565→
   566→	require.True(t, env.FileExists("overlap_test.go"))
   567→	originalContent := env.ReadFile("overlap_test.go")
   568→	t.Logf("Original content: %s", originalContent)
   569→
   570→	// Verify rewind points exist (session tracked the change)
   571→	points := env.GetRewindPoints()
   572→	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(points), 1, "Should have rewind points")
   573→
   574→	// User reverts the file and writes completely different content
   575→	t.Log("User reverting file and writing different content")
   576→	differentContent := `package main
   577→
   578→func CompletelyDifferent() string {
   579→	return "user wrote this, not the agent"
   580→}
   581→`
   582→	env.WriteFile("overlap_test.go", differentContent)
   583→
   584→	// Verify content is different
   585→	currentContent := env.ReadFile("overlap_test.go")
   586→	assert.NotEqual(t, originalContent, currentContent)
   587→
   588→	// Commits before this test
   589→	commitsBefore := env.GetCommitCount()
   590→
   591→	// User commits the different content
   592→	t.Log("Committing user-written content")
   593→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add overlap test file", "overlap_test.go")
   594→
   595→	// Verify commit was made
   596→	commitsAfter := env.GetCommitCount()
   597→	assert.Equal(t, commitsBefore+1, commitsAfter, "Should have one new commit")
   598→
   599→	// Check for checkpoint trailer
   600→	// With content-aware overlap detection, if the user completely replaced
   601→	// the agent's content (new file with different hash), there should be
   602→	// NO checkpoint trailer added. This is documented in checkpoint-scenarios.md
   603→	// under "Content-Aware Overlap Detection".
   604→	checkpointIDs := env.GetAllCheckpointIDsFromHistory()
   605→	t.Logf("Checkpoint IDs found: %v", checkpointIDs)
   606→
   607→	// The first commit (Initial commit from NewFeatureBranchEnv) doesn't have a checkpoint.
   608→	// Only agent-assisted commits should have checkpoint trailers.
   609→	// When user completely replaces agent content, content-aware detection should
   610→	// prevent the checkpoint trailer from being added.
   611→	//
   612→	// Per docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md:
   613→	// - New file + content hash mismatch → No overlap → No checkpoint trailer
   614→	assert.Empty(t, checkpointIDs,
   615→		"Content-aware detection should prevent checkpoint trailer when user completely replaces agent content")
   616→}

# Create a temp test to see what Claude creates
TMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
cd "$TMP_DIR"
git init
git config user.email "test@test.com"

echo "test" > README.md
git add . && git commit -m "init"
mkdir -p .claude
cat > .claude/settings.json << 'EOF'
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [{ "matcher": "", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "echo HOOK_SESSION_START >> /tmp/hook_test.log" }] }],
    "UserPromptSubmit": [{ "matcher": "", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "echo HOOK_USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT >> /tmp/hook_test.log" }] }],
    "Stop": [{ "matcher": "", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "echo HOOK_STOP >> /tmp/hook_test.log" }] }]
  }
}
EOF
rm -f /tmp/hook_test.log

echo "=== First prompt ==="
claude --model haiku --session-id $(uuidgen) -p "Say hello" 2>&1
echo ""
echo "=== Hook log after first prompt ==="
cat /tmp/hook_test.log 2>/dev/null || echo "(no log)"

echo ""
echo "=== Second prompt ==="
claude --model haiku --session-id $(uuidgen) -p "Say goodbye" 2>&1
echo ""
echo "=== Hook log after second prompt ==="
cat /tmp/hook_test.log 2>/dev/null || echo "(no log)"

rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"
